title: CLI agent telemetry signet proposal
content:
Context and intent:

This is a personal proposal / working notes for a light-weight client (CLI) agent telemetry flow that balances debug observability with user privacy and tamper-evidence. The key idea is a small, short-lived cryptographic marker called a "signet" that the local agent mints per-session and attaches to telemetry envelopes. The signet proves the telemetry was produced by the agent runtime and carries the consent & sampling provenance.

Goals:
- Allow engineers to collect actionable client-side signals for debugging and performance analysis (latency histograms, cold-start markers, config mashups) without shipping raw PII or long-term device IDs.
- Make client telemetry auditable and tamper-evident with minimal crypto (HMAC-based signet).
- Provide a simple opt-in/opt-out config surface and a sampling policy that can be updated remotely.
- Keep payloads small and compatible with existing ingest endpoints (hosted API route).

Core concepts:
- signet: base64(HMAC(agent-session-key, session-metadata || nonce || timestamp)) plus short plaintext metadata about consent and sample_reason. 16-24 byte HMAC output encoded to base64 (trimmed) to stay small.
- session-metadata: ephemeral, includes agent version, runtime-id (ephemeral), and telemetry-level (none/min/basic/verbose).
- sample_reason: a short tag explaining why this session was sampled (manual, error-trigger, rollout, diagnostic).
- telemetry-envelope: compact JSON with envelope-level redaction rules; fields are enumerated below.

Telemetry envelope (shape sketch - textual JSON snippet):
{
  "envelope_version": "v1",
  "session": {
    "agent_version": "0.8.3",
    "runtime_id": "r-Ab12cd",
    "telemetry_level": "basic"
  },
  "signet": {
    "value": "b64-hmac-trim",
    "nonce": "n-0001",
    "ts": "2026-01-22T14:22:00Z",
    "sample_reason": "error-trigger"
  },
  "payload": {
    "events": [ /* small array of events, each event is a small map */ ],
    "metrics": { /* numeric buckets */ }
  },
  "redaction": {
    "fields_removed": [ /* names of fields removed before sending */ ]
  }
}

Redaction rules (principles):
- Never include full user identifiers (email, device-id, account-id). Replace with hashed or first-2-chars+hash-fragment patterns if needed for correlation (but default: omit).
- Truncate long strings ( > 256 chars ) and record truncation marker.
- Local exception: if user explicitly opts into "support-mode", a secure ephemeral token may be produced that allows linking to a support session for up to 24 hours.

Signet lifecycle and validation (notes):
- Generation: agent derives a session HMAC key from a persistent machine key (rotating) + session nonce. HMAC(key, agent_version||runtime_id||nonce||ts||telemetry_level).
- TTL: signet TTL is short (e.g., 24 hours). Agents rotate signet per major action (install, restart, config-change).
- Server-side validation: ingest pipeline knows the public-ish mapping of agent builds -> secret rotation windows (we can't store per-device secrets server-side). Validation is lightweight: if HMAC validates against a small set of allowed keys for that agent_version window, accept; otherwise mark as unverifiable but accept payload if policy allows, tagging it as "unverifiable-signet".
- Auditability: signet value + sample_reason + ts are recorded in ingestion logs for later sampling review.

API shapes and routes (draft):
- POST /v1/agent-telemetry (accepts envelope, 2MB limit but target << 10KB typically)
  - headers: Authorization: Bearer <api-key> (existing client API keys), X-Agent-Signet: <signature-compact> (optional redundancy)
  - body: telemetry-envelope JSON
  - response 202: {"ingest_id": "ing-123", "status": "queued"}

- GET /v1/agent-telemetry/config (agent polls for sampling and redaction policy)
  - response: {"telemetry_level": "basic", "sampling_rate": 0.01, "allow_support_mode": true, "policy_version": "2026-01-21-v2"}

Sampling policy examples:
- default: 1% basic telemetry, 0.1% verbose
- error-trigger: immediate sample of the session with sample_reason="error-trigger" for next N events (N=20)
- rollout debug: if agent is in a canary group, increase to 10% basic, 2% verbose

Local agent config (YAML sketch to include in dotfiles):
agent:
  telemetry_level: basic # none|min|basic|verbose
  enable_support_mode: false
  sampling_overrides:
    error-trigger: 1.0
    rollout: 0.1
  signet_key_rotation_days: 7

Sequence diagram (text):
Agent start -> generate runtime_id and signet
Agent -> Ingest: POST /v1/agent-telemetry (envelope with signet)
Ingest -> validate signet against known rotation windows
If valid -> enqueue to telemetry pipeline with tag signet_verified:true
If invalid -> enqueue as signet_verified:false and tag for manual audit if sample_reason != "manual"

Privacy backstops and opt-out:
- Agent honors an OS-level or environment variable opt-out (REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0).
- Agents must expose a one-line command: "redis-cli-agent telemetry status|enable|disable" (name TBD) for support & developer workflows.
- Retention: client telemetry stored for 30 days by default; long-term retention only on explicit product/enterprise contract.

Operational notes and telemetry costs:
- Keep envelopes small: prefer counters and small event tags rather than verbose text.
- Use server-side sampling to cut downstream costs; server can drop verbose payloads while keeping basic markers.

Open questions / TODOs (personal backlog):
- Decide exact HMAC algorithm and key rotation cadence (HMAC-SHA256 vs HKDF pre-derive). Tradeoffs: ease of implementation vs key-size.
- How to provision the small key material in Private deployments? Options: customer-managed KMS wrap, local-only key without server validation (but then signet unverifiable).
- UX for support_mode: how to ensure users intentionally enable and can revoke quickly?
- Map to existing ingest quotas and rate-limiters so client bursts don't trigger mass rejection during canaries.
- Add example Rust/Go snippet for signet generation and a small JS shim for CLI wrappers.

Quick prototype cURL (example):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/agent-telemetry \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '"<envelope-json>"'

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc lightweight. If/when this matures, move to a formal design doc in shared_drives/engineering/developer-experience/ and add a PR to GH repo with examples.
- Ping Jonah for a quick design pairing session to prototype the Rust bits.

-- Asha
